I like to think of my life
as cups.

Three of them, filled in order (most days). First, what needs to be done. Then, my soul. Then everything outside me that feeds it, until the cup runs over onto my people.

click to jump in!1. Filling my own cupOn paper: the degree, the projects, the ground I stand on click for a sip2. More than halfMy soul: taste, stories, the films and books that made me click & pour3. To the brim, and overCommunity, inspiration, and the people who get what spills over

"What makes you get out of bed every morning?"

I first heard that question on a podcast, and it quietly changed the way I think about passion.

Mine looks different every day. Underneath, it's always the same thing: becoming the woman I picture fifteen years from now.

So every morning, I go outside and do one small thing for her. The days look different. The vision never does.

Some days

Eleven hours in the library for digital logic, counting caches.

Some days

Choosing the outfit that makes me feel like her.

Sometimes

A café, and the first hello to the stranger building something across the table. (Just ask my three neighbourhood cafés. At this point, the coffee is often on the house.)

Sometimes

Simply being there for my friends.

Cup 01 · Filling my own cup

What I do to fill my own cup.

Before anything else, I need solid ground. Engineering is how I prove to myself that I am enough. It's where my confidence comes from: the kind that lets me move forward, trust my own decisions, and know they're informed ones. Everything else gets poured on top.

Things I've built

01 Capstone · AI Raise Lab A telepresence robot for students who can't be physically on campus

Automating a telepresence robot so students with accessibility needs can still live the campus experience, remotely. We're pairing a Velodyne VLP-16 LiDAR with a Raspberry Pi running ROS2 Humble in Docker, and building SLAM, localization and obstacle avoidance. I coordinate our team of five.

02 Custom CPU design A 16-bit CPU, and its clock

Designed from the ground up in Logisim: a multi-stage pipeline with ALU, register file, data memory and branching logic, all run by a custom finite state machine.

03 Project manager A multifunctional robot, in three weeks

Led a team of six to design and deliver three robotics subsystems on a three-week clock. Gantt charts for time, a budget model for cost, and Python tuned for real-time performance on embedded hardware.

Where I've put it to work

ETIYA · Business Analyst intern Videotron's digital transformation of CSR services

I sat between the client and the builders, turning Videotron's customer needs into technical solutions across cross-functional Agile teams. The real work was hearing what stakeholders actually needed, then telling that story so business and tech could move as one.

"The biggest and most valuable project you will ever work on is yourself."

Cup 02 · More than half

The rest is taste.

Once my mind is fed, I fill the rest with what makes me, me: style, beauty in ordinary places, moments worth keeping, and the stories I tell about them.

If a film crew followed me for a day…

(First, they'd have to be up at 6am.)

6:00Getting dressed the way Harvey Specter would.
MorningThe to-do list, and every deadline sized up.
DayOne of my three usual cafés, getting everything done. Somewhere between tasks I'll run into at least five friends, and leave every conversation with a new idea.
20:00Home with my 8pm americano, watching my favourite YouTubers for inspiration and daydreaming about who I’m becoming. Unless it’s exam season. Then it’s studying, endlessly.

"I think a lot about the difference between looking at something and actually seeing it."

Places, people, objects, and the rhythm each one moves at
Cup 03 · To the brim, and over

Full enough to pour.

Then comes everything that fills me from the outside: the rooms I build, the people I learn from, the friends I share my life with. It fills the cup to the brim, and a full cup only has one place to go. It spills over, onto my people. When I lost my footing in university, pouring into other people's cups is what kept mine full.

Rooms I've built

I've never had "founder" in my title, but I've always started things.

POWE · VP ConferenceA day on campus for future women engineers

Planned and ran POWE's annual conference for CEGEP students, with tours of research labs chosen by interest and panels with leaders from sponsors like Airbus and Bombardier.

160students · 9 labs
Sympowesium · Organizing teamTwo days, made into one better one

Helped deliver the first-ever one-day edition for McGill women in engineering. I shaped the research, industry, AI & tech and internship panels, and designed a gift for every guest.

150+students · 80+ pros
ECSESS · VP AdminElected by my peers

Co-chair of our weekly council meetings and owner of department merch, from design to sales. I replaced a one-Google-Form-at-a-time process with a real online store.

250+students a semester
Women in Tech · VP MediaGrowing the room, online

Owned outreach and account growth, leading a team of four. One Instagram campaign I ran brought in 25 new coordinator applications in five days.

+6.25%reach in my first 30 days

People who inspire me

Mel Robbins

In my first year, alone and on the academic struggle bus, she was the voice in my head telling me to keep going. She brought me back.

Emma Grede

Ask me who I want to be when I grow up, and the answer is her. I would give anything to be her assistant, even for a week.

John Ternus

My bond with Apple began the day my dad brought home an iPhone 4S, the first touchscreen phone to ever enter our apartment. It's one of the reasons I chose engineering: I wrote about it in the essays that got me into some of the world's best engineering schools, and I meant every word. I admire how he built his way up through hard work and grit, all the way to the top.

"Never be the smartest person in the room. If you are, you're in the wrong room."

Your network is your net worth
And what spills over…

Ask my friends, they'll say…

The do-erThe planner. The one who makes things happen.
The quiet protectorEvery need is seen, every voice is heard, and no one is left out of the room.
The linkerIf two people can solve something for each other, I'm the one who introduces them.

What I've learned from them

I can name one trait I admire in each of my closest friends, and I study how they live so I can carry it with me.

[ Friend ]How to turn a tough moment into an advantage, and answer with strategy.
[ Friend ]How to dream big and still make time for everything, and everyone.
[ Friend ]That sometimes you plant both feet and do the hard, technical work. No shortcuts.

"Pouring into other people's cups kept mine full."
